title: geo-score watch config (geo-score-watch.json)
description: The file `geo_score.py watch` and the MCP server read: the brand and competitors to look for in answers, the question file, the engines and the spending caps. What `watch check` refuses in this file, the schema refuses too, except what a schema cannot state: engine ids and competitor names must be unique. Elsewhere it is stricter. `watch check` warns about a key it does not know and ignores it; this schema rejects one, so an editor flags a mistyped cap such as `budget` for `budget_usd` before a paid run. It also types values `watch check` takes as they come, such as a domain that is not a string or an empty model name. `watch check`, like JSON Schema, takes 2.0 as an integer.

$schema.description: The URL of this schema. `watch init` writes it, so editors validate and complete the file.

brand.description: You: what counts as your citation and your mention.

competitors.description: Tracked competitors. Names must differ from each other and from the brand.

queries.description: The question file, relative to this file: a CSV with the columns query_id,query and optionally intent_tier,target_url,branded.

engines.description: The engines to ask. Omitted or null: ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini and Claude through their APIs, with the default model of the running release; `watch init` writes the models out.

country.description: Two-letter ISO code passed to the engines that accept a location, or null (an empty string also means none).

max_calls.description: Exact cap on the questions asked in one run. A plan above it does not start.

budget_usd.description: Spend cap in USD, checked before every call; it can be exceeded by at most one call per engine. null: no budget.

prices.description: Per engine id, USD, for the engines whose provider does not report the cost of a call.

strings.description: One string, or a list of strings.

domains.description: Domains that count as this entity's; subdomains count too.

url_prefixes.description: URL prefixes that count as this entity's, such as a store or profile on someone else's site.

aliases.description: Other names an answer may use.

id.description: Unique engine id; defaults to the provider name.

model.description: Defaults to the provider's default model in the running release.

base_url.description: A compatible endpoint: https://, or http://localhost.

api.description: Gemini only: the Interactions API (the default) or generateContent.

key_env.description: The environment variable that holds the key, instead of the provider's usual one. Never the key itself.
